subject: Non-resident GST handling for Aqualis — invoice flow & self-billing options
messages:
From: Keiko Tanaka <keiko.tanaka@aqualis.jp>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aqualis.jp
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0900
Subject: GST treatment for non-resident supplier (Redwood invoice 000852)

Hi Jasmine,

Quick question from our AP procurement team — Aqualis is a Japanese VAT-registered buyer, and we are checking whether Redwood (a non-resident supplier) can be invoiced without Japanese consumption tax if we apply the reverse-charge/self-billing regime.

We received Invoice_20260630_Redwood_000852.pdf but it currently shows a 10% consumption tax line. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- re-issue the invoice zero-rated (no CT) with a reverse-charge note, OR
- sign a self-billing agreement so we can account for the CT on our side and you issue a net invoice?

Attached: Aqualis_GST_Registration_Proof_202606.pdf (our business tax certificate).

Need to get this into AP accounts by July 5th — can you advise next steps and what docs you need from us?

Thanks,
Keiko
Procurement, Aqualis Inc.

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Keiko Tanaka <keiko.tanaka@aqualis.jp>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: GST treatment for non-resident supplier (Redwood invoice 000852)

Hi Keiko — thanks for flagging this. Short answer: we can support either approach, but we need to validate Aqualis's tax registration and agree an amendment for self-billing if you want us to issue net invoices.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please confirm the legal entity name on the tax cert matches the PO (you have done this — thanks).
2) Marcus (cc'd) will confirm our recommended tax treatment (reverse-charge vs export of services) based on our AP tax counsel.
3) If you want self-billing, sign the DocuSign amendment (link below) and we'll re-issue Invoice_20260630_Redwood_000852.pdf as a net invoice with a reverse-charge annotation.
4) If you prefer not to sign self-billing, we can reissue with a line showing 0% consumption tax and a note: "Reverse charge - recipient liable under Japanese tax law" — but we need your confirmation in writing.

I attach the current invoice for reference and I've asked Finance to hold any collection until this is resolved so there's no double charging.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/link/amendment-msa-aqualis
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-aqualis-invoice

I'll hand over to Marcus for tax recommendation.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Keiko Tanaka <keiko.tanaka@aqualis.jp>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 02:18:00 +0000
Subject: RE: GST treatment for non-resident supplier (Redwood invoice 000852)

Hi Keiko / Jasmine — reviewed with tax counsel. Practical guidance:
- For Japanese consumption tax, non-resident supply of digital/SAAS services can be zero-rated where the recipient is a registered business and is required to self-assess (reverse-charge).
- We need the tax registration number (you provided), company name, and confirmation that Aqualis will account for the consumption tax.

Recommendation: sign the self-billing amendment so Redwood can issue net (no-consumption-tax) invoices with the following annotation: "Tax: Reverse charge — recipient to self-assess under Japanese Consumption Tax law; no consumption tax charged by supplier." This avoids us having to collect and remit CT and is cleaner for month-end.

Operational asks for Aqualis to speed the change:
- Signed DocuSign amendment (link already shared)
- PO/PO number to map to re-issued invoice (please confirm PO#)
- Confirmation email from procurement stating you accept reverse-charge accounting for this supplier.

We'll put a one-off hold on collection for invoice 000852 until we re-issue. If you need a credit note + re-issue, we'll process that once the self-billing amendment is signed.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Tax Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Keiko Tanaka <keiko.tanaka@aqualis.jp>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aqualis.jp
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 10:08:00 +0900
Subject: Re: GST treatment for non-resident supplier (Redwood invoice 000852)

Thanks Marcus — we can proceed with self-billing. Confirming:
- PO#: AQL-2026-1107 (please map on re-issued invoice)
- Aqualis will self-assess consumption tax for Redwood services and provide any evidence required for audit.
- Procurement will sign the DocuSign amendment today and send confirmation mail after signing.

I've attached our tax registration PDF again for your records and procurement will send the DocuSign signed copy by EOD. Let me know if Redwood needs any specific wording on the signed amendment.

Best,
Keiko

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Keiko Tanaka <keiko.tanaka@aqualis.jp>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Confirmation: self-billing amendment received & invoice reissue plan

Hi Keiko — thanks for the quick turnaround. Monica from Finance here. Procurement's signed amendment received (DocuSign completed). Action plan:
1) We'll issue Credit Note CN-00021 to cancel Invoice_20260630_Redwood_000852.pdf (to avoid dual charge).
2) Re-issue Invoice_20260703_Redwood_000852_NET.pdf (net amount, no consumption tax) and annotate: "Reverse charge — recipient to self-assess under Japanese Consumption Tax law. PO#: AQL-2026-1107".
3) We'll email the new invoice and a PDF copy to procurement@aqualis.jp and accounts-payable@aqualis.jp.
4) Collection hold lifted once re-issued invoice sent (we will not send collection reminders for the cancelled invoice).

Attachments: CreditNote_CN-00021_stub.pdf (will attach final PDF in follow-up)

If you need any alternate wording on the invoice for your internal auditors, reply to this thread and we can adjust before re-issue.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
